alerts.name: SQL Injection
alerts.desc: SQL injection may allow an attacker to view, modify or delete database contents, bypass authentication mechanisms, and execute administrative operations on the database server.

instances.evidence: You have an error in your SQL syntax near ''1'='1'
instances.otherinfo: Boolean-based SQL injection detected on parameter 'id'

alerts.solution: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database operations. Implement strict input validation.

alerts.name: Remote OS Command Injection
alerts.desc: The application passes unvalidated user input directly to a system shell, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on the operating system hosting the application.

instances.otherinfo: Direct command execution observed in response payload.

alerts.solution: Avoid invoking shell processes with user inputs. If required, use parameterized system APIs with strict whitelisting.

alerts.name: Cross-Site Scripting (Reflected)
alerts.desc: User input supplied via request parameters is included in immediate HTML output without proper contextual encoding, enabling execution of arbitrary client-side scripts.

instances.otherinfo: Reflected in search results title container.

alerts.solution: Contextually encode all untrusted inputs before inserting them into HTML, JavaScript, CSS, or URL attributes.

alerts.name: Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens
alerts.desc: A state-changing form submission does not include an unpredictable anti-CSRF token, allowing attackers to execute unauthorized actions on behalf of authenticated users.

instances.otherinfo: Target form contains sensitive email change fields.

alerts.solution: Implement unique, cryptographically strong anti-CSRF synchronization tokens on all state-changing requests and enforce SameSite=Lax cookie attribute.

alerts.alert: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
alerts.desc: The server response lacks a Content-Security-Policy header, reducing defense-in-depth protection against cross-site scripting (XSS) and data exfiltration.
alerts.solution: Configure a strict Content Security Policy HTTP response header specifying allowed script, object, and style sources.

alerts.name: Cookie No HttpOnly Flag
alerts.desc: A session cookie was set without the HttpOnly attribute, allowing client-side scripts to read session identifiers via document.cookie during an XSS attack.

instances.otherinfo: Session cookie is accessible to JavaScript.

alerts.solution: Set the HttpOnly and Secure flags on all sensitive and session cookies.

alerts.name: Application Error Disclosure
alerts.desc: The application returns raw internal error details and database exception messages, exposing internal system paths and framework versions to potential attackers.

instances.evidence: Exception in thread 'main' java.sql.SQLException: column 'admin' does not exist

alerts.solution: Disable verbose error messages in production and display generic error pages while logging details to secure internal logs.
